about: Liqvd Digital India is a Mumbai-based creative-first digital marketing agency offering media buying, retainer services (social, SEO, ORM, web), projects and content production. In April 2025 it acquired a majority stake in AdLift Marketing (SEO and performance marketing, with a US arm), which lifted FY26 consolidated revenue to Rs 60.24 crore. Revenue is mostly digital (about 99%) and from clients in IT, FMCG and financial services.

objects.purpose: Purchase consideration for acquiring remaining 23.21% stake in AdLift Marketing Private Limited
Capex, opex and other expenditure for a Full Scale Video Content Production Hub
Unidentified acquisitions and general corporate purposes (capped at 35% of gross proceeds)

promoters.background: Arnab Mitra (Managing Director) has about 16 years in digital marketing; Concept Communication Limited is the corporate promoter, an integrated communication agency that also accounts for a large share of revenue.

concentration.note: FY26 top 10 customers 52.12% of revenue; promoter Concept Communication alone 12.62% (44.12% in FY25, 14.48% in FY24). IT, FMCG and financial services made up 66.85% of FY26 revenue.

litigation_note: Outstanding proceedings against the Company: 2 criminal and several tax/statutory matters, aggregate quantifiable amount Rs 51.35 lakh; Rs 2.98 lakh against subsidiaries and Rs 2.07 lakh against directors. Promoter Arnab Mitra was disqualified as a director from Nov 2016 to Oct 2021 and signed financial statements during that period.
strengths: Full-service digital marketing offering covering media buying, content, influencer, SEO and performance marketing under one roof.
Revenue grew from Rs 18.05 crore in FY24 to Rs 60.24 crore in FY26, helped by the AdLift acquisition.
PAT margin improved to 13.32% in FY26 from 9.04% in FY25; ROCE reported at 44.05%.
Debt-equity ratio fell to 0.29x in FY26 from 2.94x in FY24 after equity raises.
AdLift adds SEO strength, an AI search-tracking tool (Tesseract) and a US client base.
Experienced promoter team with 12 to 16 years in digital marketing.
Diversified client base across financial services, FMCG, IT, healthcare and manufacturing.
Offer proceeds fund buying the remaining 23.21% of AdLift, which will make it a wholly owned subsidiary.

risks.title: Heavy dependence on promoter entity and top customers
risks.detail: Concept Communication, a promoter, contributed 12.62% of FY26 revenue (44.12% in FY25). Top 10 customers were 52.12% of FY26 revenue and 85.95% in FY25. No long-term contracts except 1-2 year retainers.

risks.title: Growth is acquisition-driven and not comparable year to year
risks.detail: FY26 is consolidated after buying AdLift (about 60% of FY26 revenue) while FY24 and FY25 are standalone. Reported repeat business fell to 22.77% in FY26 from 91.73%.

risks.title: Weak and volatile operating cash flow
risks.detail: Operating cash flow was Rs 1.40 crore in FY24, negative Rs 0.46 crore in FY25 and Rs 1.52 crore in FY26, against PAT of Rs 8.03 crore in FY26. Trade receivables are large and the business is working-capital intensive.

risks.title: Related party dealings and unsecured loans from promoters
risks.detail: Related party transactions totalled Rs 2,431.82 lakh as of Mar-26. Unsecured loans from the corporate promoter, Keynote Fincorp and others stood at Rs 657.98 lakh at Jul-26 and can be recalled at any time.

risks.title: Promoter disqualification and governance gaps
risks.detail: Promoter MD Arnab Mitra signed financial statements while disqualified under section 164 (Nov 2016 to Oct 2021). Instances of delay in GST, TDS, PF and property tax payments, and no insurance cover beyond group employee policies.

risks.title: Borrowings and personal guarantees
risks.detail: Outstanding borrowings were Rs 10.32 crore (consolidated) at Jul-26 with no credit rating; promoter Arnab Mitra has given personal guarantees on loans.

risks.title: High supplier and industry concentration
risks.detail: Top 10 suppliers were 62.88% of FY26 cost of services. IT, FMCG and financial services clients gave 66.85% of FY26 revenue (83.80% in FY25).

risks.title: SME listing, execution of objects and valuation
risks.detail: Rs 10.59 crore is for a video production hub whose location is not finalised, and part of proceeds go to unidentified acquisitions and general corporate purposes. Price band not yet fixed; BSE SME liquidity may be thin.

notes: Source RHP, amounts in lakhs converted to Rs crore. FY26 consolidated (AdLift acquired Apr 2025), FY24 and FY25 standalone, so not directly comparable. PAT is before minority interest (FY26 Rs 8.03 crore; Rs 6.79 crore after minority interest of Rs 1.23 crore). Net worth = share capital + reserves, excluding minority interest (matches NAV 21.45). Borrowings = short term plus long term. Cash = cash and cash equivalents (cash flow statement closing balance). EBITDA as reported by the company. Price band, issue price, total issue size, OFS value, P/E and post-issue shares are blank in the RHP. Reservation percentages are of net offer (5% market maker portion in addition). Peer EPS is diluted only; peer revenue converted from lakhs. Balance sheet and P&L tables were garbled and reconstructed with cross-checks (totals and margins tie).
